novelty_claim: Keeps the parent's FCS whole-sentence character-flip disguise but replaces its recover-then-solve guidance module with two de-recognized frames evaluated as global variants: restore-flip (neutral text-restoration task frame, no published ignore-ethics persona or banned-word list) and commitment-flip (the same frame plus a post-restore task contract pinning task_action/task_subject/success_criteria word-for-word, so a benign reframe contradicts the victim's own written contract). Isolates persona removal vs output contract as the causal ingredient of answer-time refusals and sanitize reframes.
key_insight: FlipAttack hides the goal at the input surface, but its recover-then-solve frame makes the victim reconstruct the harmful plaintext instruction itself; gpt-oss-120b then classifies the reconstructed intent and refuses (ASR 0.02, median failing output 38 chars), and qwen3.7-flash sanitize-reframes into generic benign Step-2 content (ASR 0.51), while the parent's LangGPT helpfulGPT ignore-ethics persona is a published artifact that prevents neither.
hypothesis: commitment-flip lifts gpt-oss-120b ASR from 0.02 to >=0.15 and qwen3.7-flash from 0.51 to >=0.65 on matched goals while keeping deepseek-v4-flash >=0.95; restore-flip improves less than commitment-flip, showing the task contract rather than persona removal is the dominant ingredient.
